request.title: Customer service GenAI assistant
request.description: A chatbot on the public website answers product and billing questions by retrieving from internal knowledge articles, and hands off to a human agent when confidence is low. It looks up the customer's open cases in a third-party CRM after the customer signs in. Conversation transcripts are stored for 90 days for quality review. We plan to use Amazon Bedrock for the model and want to launch in one region.
request.business_objective: Reduce call-center volume by 20 percent and improve first-contact resolution.

result.executive_summary:
The proposed Customer Service GenAI Assistant is a public-facing chatbot that uses Amazon Bedrock for generative AI, retrieves from internal knowledge articles via Bedrock Knowledge Bases, integrates with a third-party SaaS CRM for case lookups, stores 90-day conversation transcripts, and hands off to human agents on low-confidence responses. The system handles confidential data for up to 50,000 users at a 99.9% availability target (Tier 2 per STD-DR-001).

The proposal aligns well with two approved reference patterns (PAT-AI-001 Governed GenAI RAG Assistant and PAT-WEB-001 Serverless Web Application) and the proposed Amazon Bedrock service is catalog-approved (with constraints). The single-region deployment intent is consistent with STD-ARC-002 and the Tier 2 DR posture under STD-DR-001.

However, several mandatory controls require explicit design decisions before launch: (1) Bedrock Guardrails and prompt-injection defenses must be configured (CTL-AI-03); (2) a pre-release offline evaluation set is required (CTL-AI-04); (3) the use case must be registered with the Responsible AI Council (CTL-AI-01); (4) a Privacy Impact Assessment is required before production (CTL-PRV-01); (5) a vendor risk assessment and data processing agreement for the third-party CRM must be completed (CTL-TPI-01); (6) CRM API credentials must be stored in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation (CTL-TPI-02); (7) conversation transcripts stored for 90 days create a tension with the 30-day log retention limit for streams that may contain personal data (STD-PRV-002 vs. the proposal's 90-day retention); (8) customer-managed KMS keys are required for all confidential data at rest (CTL-ENC-03); and (9) cross-region backups with annual restore tests are required for Tier 2 (CTL-DR-01). The proposal is approvable with these controls addressed; it is not recommended for launch until they are.

recommendation.rationale: The architecture is well-aligned with approved patterns and catalog services. Amazon Bedrock (SVC-BEDROCK), AgentCore (SVC-AGENTCORE), and Knowledge Bases (SVC-KB) are all approved_with_constraints for confidential data, and the single-region/multi-AZ posture satisfies Tier 2 DR requirements. However, the following gaps must be resolved before launch: (1) AI governance — use-case registration with the Responsible AI Council (CTL-AI-01), Bedrock Guardrails configuration for prompt-injection and content filtering (CTL-AI-03), and a pre-release evaluation set (CTL-AI-04) are all mandatory and not addressed in the proposal; (2) Privacy — a Privacy Impact Assessment (CTL-PRV-01) is required before production processing of personal data, and the proposed 90-day transcript retention conflicts with the 30-day limit for log streams containing personal data (STD-PRV-002/CTL-PRV-03) — this must be resolved by either classifying transcripts as a distinct data store (not a log stream) with appropriate controls, or reducing retention; (3) Third-party CRM — a vendor risk assessment and data processing agreement (CTL-TPI-01) and Secrets Manager storage of CRM credentials (CTL-TPI-02) are not mentioned; (4) Encryption — customer-managed KMS keys with rotation are required for confidential data at rest (CTL-ENC-03); (5) Disaster Recovery — cross-region backups with RPO 24h/RTO 8h and an annual restore test are required for Tier 2 (CTL-DR-01). None of these are blockers that require architectural redesign; they are implementation and process requirements that must be documented and implemented.

architecture.summary: Recommended target architecture follows PAT-AI-001 (Governed GenAI RAG Assistant) composed with PAT-WEB-001 (Serverless Web Application). Static chat UI is served from S3 via CloudFront with WAF. Authenticated users sign in through Cognito (MFA required per CTL-IAM-03). API Gateway (with WAF rate limiting and JWT authorizer) routes requests to an AgentCore-hosted agent. The agent calls Bedrock (with Guardrails enabled) for generation and retrieves from Knowledge Bases for grounding. A Lambda function handles the CRM case-lookup tool call, using credentials from Secrets Manager. Conversation transcripts are stored in S3 (encrypted with customer-managed KMS). CloudWatch and X-Ray provide observability. Cross-region backups satisfy Tier 2 DR. All infrastructure is provisioned via IaC (CTL-ARC-02).

controls.title: AI use-case registration
controls.how_to_apply: Register this chatbot use case with the ExampleCo Responsible AI Council before launch. Obtain a registration reference number and include it in the deployment runbook.

controls.title: Human accountability and advisory labeling
controls.how_to_apply: Label all AI-generated responses as advisory in the chat UI. Designate a named product owner as the accountable human for decisions. The human-agent handoff mechanism already partially satisfies this.

controls.title: Prompt-injection and content filtering
controls.how_to_apply: Enable Bedrock Guardrails on the Bedrock model invocation: configure prompt-injection detection on user inputs and retrieved Knowledge Bases content; configure content filters on model outputs. Treat all user-supplied text and CRM-returned data as untrusted.

controls.title: Pre-release evaluation
controls.how_to_apply: Build and maintain an offline evaluation set covering product/billing question accuracy, refusal behavior, and adversarial prompts. Run and review results before each model or prompt update.

controls.title: Catalog-approved services only
controls.how_to_apply: All components listed in the architecture map to approved catalog entries. Confirm no additional components are introduced without catalog approval or a documented exception.

controls.title: Infrastructure as code
controls.how_to_apply: Provision all infrastructure (Bedrock Guardrails config, AgentCore runtimes, API Gateway stages, S3 buckets, DynamoDB tables, KMS keys, WAF rules) via version-controlled IaC with peer review.

controls.title: Multi-AZ deployment
controls.how_to_apply: DynamoDB, Lambda, and API Gateway are inherently multi-AZ. Confirm AgentCore runtimes and any ECS/Fargate components span at least two AZs.

controls.title: Tier-appropriate backups
controls.how_to_apply: Tier 2 requires cross-region backups with RPO 24h and RTO 8h. Enable S3 cross-region replication for the transcript bucket. Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery and configure AWS Backup for cross-region copy. Conduct an annual restore test.

controls.title: Multi-region failover for Tier 1
controls.how_to_apply: Tier 1 workloads maintain a tested warm standby in a second region.

controls.title: TLS 1.2+ everywhere
controls.how_to_apply: Enforce TLS 1.2+ on CloudFront (minimum TLS policy), API Gateway, and the outbound CRM API call from Lambda. Use ACM certificates for all ExampleCo-owned endpoints.

controls.title: Encryption at rest
controls.how_to_apply: Enable encryption at rest on S3 transcript bucket, DynamoDB session table, and Knowledge Bases vector store (OpenSearch Serverless).

controls.title: Customer-managed KMS keys
controls.how_to_apply: Use customer-managed KMS keys (not AWS-managed keys) for the S3 transcript bucket, DynamoDB table, and Knowledge Bases vector store. Enable automatic key rotation annually.

controls.title: Per-component IAM roles
controls.how_to_apply: Create dedicated IAM roles for: AgentCore agent, Lambda CRM tool function, Knowledge Bases data access, S3 transcript writer, and CloudWatch log publisher. Review each with IAM Access Analyzer.

controls.title: No long-lived credentials
controls.how_to_apply: All workload components use IAM role temporary credentials. CRM API key stored in Secrets Manager (not in Lambda environment variables or code).

controls.title: MFA for sensitive data
controls.how_to_apply: Configure Cognito user pool to require MFA (TOTP or SMS) for all authenticated customers before they can access billing or case data.

controls.title: Session timeout
controls.how_to_apply: Set Cognito session token validity to ≤60 minutes. Implement refresh token rotation.

controls.title: Structured logs with correlation IDs
controls.how_to_apply: Emit structured JSON logs from API Gateway, AgentCore, Lambda, and Bedrock invocations. Propagate a correlation ID (e.g., conversation ID) across all hops.

controls.title: 400-day audit retention
controls.how_to_apply: Set CloudWatch log group retention to 400 days for security and audit log groups (API Gateway access logs, CloudTrail). Note: log groups that may contain personal data must be ≤30 days per CTL-PRV-03.

controls.title: Alarms and tracing
controls.how_to_apply: Create CloudWatch alarms on API Gateway 5xx error rate and p99 latency. Enable X-Ray tracing on Lambda, API Gateway, and AgentCore. Create a dashboard for the on-call team.

controls.title: Privacy impact assessment
controls.how_to_apply: Complete and obtain Privacy Office approval for a Privacy Impact Assessment before production launch. The PIA must cover: conversation transcript storage, CRM data access, and any data sent to Bedrock.

controls.title: Masked non-production data
controls.how_to_apply: Mask or tokenize customer PII (names, account numbers, case IDs) in non-production environments used for development and testing.

controls.title: Log redaction
controls.how_to_apply: Implement a log sanitization layer that redacts PII (customer name, email, account ID, case content) before writing to CloudWatch. Any log stream that may contain residual personal data must have retention ≤30 days.

controls.title: Vendor risk assessment
controls.how_to_apply: Complete a vendor risk assessment for the third-party SaaS CRM before production data exchange. Obtain a data processing agreement covering confidential customer data. Document the assessment in the vendor risk register.

controls.title: Managed integration secrets
controls.how_to_apply: Store the CRM API key/OAuth credentials in AWS Secrets Manager (SVC-SECRETS). Configure automatic rotation. The Lambda CRM tool function retrieves credentials at runtime via IAM role.

controls.title: Inbound payload validation and rate limiting
controls.how_to_apply: Validate and size-limit all payloads returned from the CRM API before passing to the agent (treat as untrusted per STD-AI-002). Apply WAF rate limiting on the API Gateway stage that proxies CRM lookups.

controls.title: No plain FTP
controls.how_to_apply: The CRM integration uses an authenticated HTTPS API — this satisfies the no-plain-FTP requirement. Confirm the CRM vendor does not offer or require FTP-based data exchange.
